title: 2001 HMMT February Calculus Problem 10
statement: Evaluate the definite integral \(\int_{-1}^{+1} \frac{2 u^{332}+u^{998}+4 u^{1664} \sin u^{691}}{1+u^{666}} \mathrm{~d} u\).

solutions.text: The term \(\frac{4 u^{1664} \sin u^{691}}{1+u^{666}}\) is odd in \(u\), so its integral is 0 . Now make the substitution \(u=v^{1 / 333} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~d} u=\frac{1}{333} v^{-332 / 333} \mathrm{~d} v\) to find that \(\int_{-1}^{+1} \frac{2 u^{332}+u^{998}}{1+u^{666}} \mathrm{~d} u=\frac{1}{333} \int_{-1}^{+1} \frac{2+v^{2}}{1+v^{2}} \mathrm{~d} v=\) \(\frac{1}{333} \int_{-1}^{+1}\left(1+\frac{1}{1+v^{2}}\right) \mathrm{d} v=\frac{2}{333} \int_{0}^{1}\left(1+\frac{1}{1+v^{2}}\right) \mathrm{d} v=\frac{2}{333}\left(1+\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+v^{2}} \mathrm{~d} v\right)=\frac{2}{333}\left(1+\tan ^{-1} 1\right)=\frac{2}{333}\left(1+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
